FROM THE EDITOR



How quickly will you deploy Quickr?
[Matthew Gervais, Associate Editor]
zbpdwark@techtarget.com

  The IBM Lotus community is buzzing about the potential collaboration capabilities of the recently released Lotus Quickr. But will this anticipation turn into adoption? Help us find out. Tell us when you plan to deploy Lotus Quickr in your Notes/Domino environment by participating in our new poll.

Whether you're still considering deploying Quickr, or already have, you'll also want to take a look at our introduction to IBM Lotus Quickr. It provides demos, articles, best practices and Web resources that will improve your understanding of what Quickr is and how to leverage it. 

If you're at the front of the adoption curve and want to share your own knowledge and insights, submit a Quickr tip to our contest for a chance to win a TomTom GO 720 Widescreen Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator!

LEARNING CENTER


Tutorial: Top 10 issues when developing Lotus Notes Domino Internet applications

  Developing external Lotus Notes Domino Internet applications (Web sites) is surprisingly different than building internal Lotus Notes Domino intranet applications. Performance, security and software configuration as well as compatibility issues must be evaluated. If these considerations are not taken into account during the development process, Lotus Notes Domino developers and administrators may face many unexpected and unpleasant post-deployment surprises. This tutorial outlines the top 10
 issues associated with developing and deploying Lotus Notes Domino Web site applications, and explains how to proactively circumvent potential problems.

A look back at Lotusphere 2008


  Whether you were one of the annual faithful attendees or not, you'll enjoy this look back at Lotusphere 2008. In this podcast, you'll hear attendees' thoughts and opinions on the upcoming releases of Lotus Notes 8.0.1 and 8.5, Lotus Quickr, and Lotus Connections.    TIP:
   
Send pop-up admin messages to Lotus Notes users from Domino Server


  Messages broadcast from the Domino Server console show up on the Lotus Notes status bar. However, the status bar text is so small that no one actually notices it. Sending admin messages in a pop-up window is a better method to notify users, because everyone in your network can see them more clearly. In this tip, SearchDomino.com member Howard Owens explains how to notify users via pop-up messages in Lotus Notes. 


   TIP:
   
How to correctly use the GetDocumentByUnid method in LotusScript


  Domino developers often use the LotusScript GetDocumentByUnid method incorrectly and receive error messages or irrelevant "ghost" documents. SearchDomino.com member Fabrice Proudhon explains the proper way to retrieve Lotus Notes documents using the GetDocumentByUnid method. 


   TIP:
   
How to execute a stored procedure in Lotus Notes Domino using Java


  Using stored procedures in Lotus Notes Domino offers a safe, portable and reliable way to build application-to-application interfaces. In this tip, SearchDomino.com member Anthony Beckford provides an example of a stored procedure written in Java that returns a Job Number value, which is then used in an executed SQL statement.
